intro: A triangular system lets each unknown depend only on earlier solutions. Follow that dependency order without forming a matrix inverse.
task: Solve lower@x=target by forward substitution and return the solution vector.
requirements: lower is a square matrix and target is a matching vector. Entries above the diagonal must have magnitude at most 1e-12 and are treated as zero.
For row i, subtract the dot product with earlier solved values, then divide by lower[i,i]. Return a new vector.
Every diagonal entry must have magnitude greater than 1e-12. Negative diagonal entries are allowed.
Raise ValueError if the requested inverse or solution exceeds finite floating-point range, even when individual inputs satisfy the bounds.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Start with the first row, which contains only one unknown, then progress downward through the system.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: At row i, subtract only coefficients multiplying previously solved entries before dividing by the diagonal.

explanation: The first row has one unknown. Each subsequent row becomes a one-variable equation once the previously solved contributions are subtracted.
Triangular solves are building blocks inside larger factorizations. They avoid the work and numerical drawbacks of explicitly constructing an inverse.
